source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: self_recursion Option
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a genuinely new mechanism found on this page: a boolean option (`{ "self_recursion": true }`) passed to couchbase.upsert()'s options argument that causes the handler's own upsert mutation to trigger another invocation of itself, letting a long-running paginated N1QL query resume across handler invocations instead of running to completion (or timing out) in a single one. Not a plain KV or N1QL concept - specific to how Eventing lets a handler checkpoint-and-continue itself.

relations.subject: eventing:self-recursion-option
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - no existing predicate captures a KV-mutation option that causes the Eventing runtime to automatically re-invoke the same handler as a continuation mechanism
relations.evidence: using self recursion results in a continuation of the query

relations.subject: cloud/eventing/eventing-handler-advancedSelfRecursion
relations.evidence: For more information about the Advanced Self-Recursion parameter, see [Optional { "self\_recursion": true }\` Parameter](eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.md#optional-params-recursion).

cross_component_finding: The example uses inline SQL++ (`SELECT name FROM \`travel-sample\`.\`inventory\`.\`hotel\` LIMIT 100 OFFSET $offset;`) purely as the workload being paginated - the self_recursion mechanism itself is a KV/upsert-option concern, not a N1QL-specific one; it would apply equally to any long-running loop inside a handler.
